title.en: Perez Hilton faces long recovery after reports he self-harmed during livestream
title.zh: 佩雷斯·希尔顿在直播中自残的报道称他面临漫长的康复期

summary.en: The US blogger is in a "serious but stable" condition in hospital, according to his family.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US blogger Perez Hilton is in a "serious but stable" condition after being admitted to hospital, according to his family.

Emergency services were called to his Miami home on Tuesday after members of the public reported concerns while watching a TikTok livestream.

The Miami sheriff's office confirmed they attended a scene of a man "livestreaming acts of self-harm" on Tuesday. They did not confirm his name but said the man was alone in the house at the time.

A statement released on the 48-year-old's website said he "experienced significant blood loss" and his treatment and recovery would be a "long process".

If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line .

The statement , external said Hilton was being held in hospital under Florida's Baker Act, which focuses on providing services for people experiencing a mental health crisis.

The father-of-three, whose real name is Mario Lavandeira, is expected to have surgery in the coming days.

A TikTok spokesman said its automated moderation systems flagged the livestream within minutes to the company's US moderation team for review.

A moderator error caused a delay in the removal, TikTok said, but the company alerted law enforcement to the situation, closed several subsequent streams within 90 seconds, and banned the account.

The pseudonym Perez Hilton is a reference to Paris Hilton who was at the height of her fame when the celebrity gossip blog was launched in 2005.

The website would go on to attract 8 million hits a day at a time when the internet was still in its relative infancy. It was criticised for vicious commentary of stars including Miley Cyrus and Lady Gaga.

He has also appeared on reality TV shows including Celebrity Rap Superstar and Celebrity Big Brother.
body.zh: 据美国博主佩雷斯·希尔顿(Perez Hilton)的家人称，他入院后病情“严重但稳定”。 周二，在公众观看 TikTok 直播时报告担忧后，紧急服务人员被呼叫到他位于迈阿密的家中。 迈阿密警长办公室证实，他们周二目睹了一名男子“现场直播自残行为”的场景。他们没有确认他的名字，但表示当时屋里只有该男子一人。 这位48岁的老人在网站上发表声明称，他“失血过多”，他的治疗和康复将是一个“漫长的过程”。 如果您受到本文中任何问题的影响，可以通过 BBC Action Line 获得帮助和支持。 外部声明称，希尔顿是根据佛罗里达州《贝克法案》被关押在医院的，该法案的重点是为经历心理健康危机的人提供服务。 这位三个孩子的父亲的真名是马里奥·拉万德拉（Mario Lavandeira），预计将在未来几天内接受手术。 TikTok 发言人表示，其自动审核系统会在几分钟内将直播标记给该公司的美国审核团队进行审核。 TikTok 表示，由于管理员错误导致删除被延迟，但该公司向执法部门通报了这一情况，在 90 秒内关闭了后续的多个流，并禁止了该帐户。 笔名佩雷斯·希尔顿 (Perez Hilton) 参考了帕丽斯·希尔顿 (Paris Hilton)，2005 年名人八卦博客推出时，帕丽斯·希尔顿 (Paris Hilton) 正处于鼎盛时期。 当互联网还处于相对起步阶段时，该网站每天的点击量达到 800 万次。它因对麦莉赛勒斯和 Lady Gaga 等明星的恶毒评论而受到批评。 他还出现在电视真人秀节目中，包括《名人说唱巨星》和《名人老大哥》。

title.en: How a schoolteacher's son became Kashmir's first India Test cricketer
title.zh: 一名教师的儿子如何成为克什米尔第一位印度测试板球运动员

summary.en: Auqib Nabi becomes Jammu and Kashmir's first cricketer to get India Test call-up, inspiring millions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Auqib smiled and replied: "One day I will reach a place where they will want to take selfies with me."

On Monday, the 29-year-old all-rounder became the first cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir to earn an India Test call-up after replacing Jasprit Bumrah in the squad for the two-match series against Sri Lanka, which starts on 15 August.

For a region where conflict, harsh winters and limited infrastructure have long restricted sporting opportunities, Auqib's selection is being seen as a landmark moment.

Raised in a small village in Baramulla district, Auqib grew up playing on local grounds with little infrastructure and few opportunities. His father, Ghulam Nabi Dar, a schoolteacher, initially wanted him to concentrate on academics and become a doctor.

"There was no scope in cricket. We used to think playing sport was a waste of time, so I insisted that Auqib focused on his studies," Ghulam says.

"After seeing his passion for cricket, I accepted it. I realised that, as a parent and a teacher, I shouldn't force him to do something he didn't want to do. I started supporting him."

Auqib's childhood friend, Junaid Dar, remembers growing up in an environment where professional cricket barely seemed possible.

"Auqib was obsessed with cricket from childhood. I used to ask him, 'Why are you doing all this? There's no future in it.' We came from a place where there was no concept of playing sport professionally and hardly any infrastructure."

To pursue his dream, Auqib regularly travelled around 70km (43 miles) to Srinagar to practise on proper cricket pitches. He did not even own a pair of spike shoes when he attended his first cricket trials.

"Auqib is very hardworking and consistent. He knows how to fight obstacles and make a way for himself.

"He would wake up early to go to the gym and then practise for the rest of the day. He did that almost every day for 10 years."

His breakthrough came in 2020 when he made his Ranji Trophy (India's top domestic tournament) debut for Jammu and Kashmir, taking a five-wicket haul against Jharkhand.

Former India all-rounder Parvez Rasool, Jammu and Kashmir's first international cricketer and Auqib's long-time captain, says one quality always stood out.

"I have followed Auqib's progress for a long time, and what stands out about him is his work ethic and discipline."

Success, however, did not come overnight. Auqib claimed 44 wickets during the 2024-25 Ranji Trophy season, finishing as the competition's leading fast bowler, but remained largely outside the national conversation.

"But we should never lose hope. Hope is what keeps the world intact. I always believed his time would come."

body.zh: 奥奇布微笑着回答：“总有一天我会到达一个他们愿意和我自拍的地方。” 周一，这位 29 岁的全能选手取代贾斯普里特·布姆拉 (Jasprit Bumrah) 参加 8 月 15 日对阵斯里兰卡的两场系列赛，成为查谟和克什米尔第一位获得印度测试征召的板球运动员。 对于一个冲突、严冬和有限的基础设施长期限制体育机会的地区来说，奥奇布的选择被视为具有里程碑意义的时刻。 奥奇布在巴拉穆拉区的一个小村庄长大，他在当地基础设施很少、机会也很少的场地上玩耍长大。他的父亲古拉姆·纳比·达尔 (Ghulam Nabi Dar) 是一名教师，最初希望他专注于学术并成为一名医生。 “板球没有发展空间。我们过去认为参加体育运动是浪费时间，所以我坚持让奥奇布专注于学习，”古拉姆说。 “看到他对板球的热情后，我接受了它。我意识到，作为家长和老师，我不应该强迫他做他不想做的事情。我开始支持他。” 奥奇布的儿时好友朱奈德·达尔 (Junaid Dar) 记得，他在一个几乎不可能参加职业板球比赛的环境中长大。 “奥奇布从小就痴迷于板球。我常常问他，‘你为什么要做这一切？这没有未来。’我们来自一个没有职业体育概念、几乎没有任何基础设施的地方。” 为了追求自己的梦想，Auqib 定期前往约 70 公里（43 英里）的斯利那加，在合适的板球场上练习。当他第一次参加板球选拔赛时，他甚至没有一双钉鞋。 “奥奇布非常勤奋，始终如一。他知道如何克服障碍，为自己开辟道路。 “他会早起去健身房，然后在一天剩下的时间里练习。十年来他几乎每天都这样做。” 他的突破出现在 2020 年，当时他在查谟和克什米尔的兰吉杯（印度顶级国内锦标赛）上首次亮相，在对阵贾坎德邦的比赛中取得了五个边门的成绩。 前印度全能运动员帕尔韦兹·拉苏尔（Parvez Rasool）是查谟和克什米尔第一位国际板球运动员，也是奥奇布的长期队长，他说有一个品质总是脱颖而出。 “我长期以来一直关注奥奇布的进步，他最突出的是他的职业道德和纪律。” 然而，成功并非一蹴而就。奥奇布在 2024-25 兰吉杯赛季中获得了 44 个三柱门，成为比赛中领先的快速投球手，但在很大程度上仍处于全国范围之外。 “但我们永远不应该失去希望。希望是让世界保持完整的动力。我一直相信他的时代会到来。” 接下来的一个赛季，Auqib 创造了兰吉杯历史上最精彩的保龄球运动之一，在 60 个三柱门中拿下……

title.en: The little-known environmental risk that could emerge as ships leave the Strait of Hormuz
title.zh: 船只离开霍尔木兹海峡可能带来的鲜为人知的环境风险

summary.en: Officials are warning that biofouling species accumulating on the hulls of ships anchored in the Strait of Hormuz could become a significant global biosecurity problem.
summary.zh: 官员警告称，停泊在霍尔木兹海峡的船只船体上附着的生物污垢物种，可能成为全球下一个重大的生物安全问题。

body.en:
The economic ramifications of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz are much discussed. But so far, the risk of ecological damage following a long blockade of ships has been overlooked.

Our recent research shows that the more than 1,500 commercial vessels that have been laid up in the Gulf since February pose a significant environmental threat because they have been accumulating marine biofouling species on their hulls.

As the strait reopens, these ships may spread these organisms to ports they visit, potentially causing an international biosecurity “super-spreader” event.

Such incursions of alien marine plants, animals, parasites and diseases affect native ecosystems and wild fisheries as well as aquaculture stocks and coastal industries. They can lead to significant environmental damage and economic losses.

But the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is not the first time shipping disruptions have resulted in significant biofouling on idle vessels.

Global merchant vessel traffic is the main mode of transport for commodities, and researchers have identified 24 choke points in maritime trade.

But 20 of these have alternative routes, meaning shipping can be managed by rerouting vessels. This can take longer and cost more but avoids mass layups.

Only four choke points have no alternative routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, the Oresund Strait in the Baltic Sea, the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits out of the Black Sea, and the Bohai Strait in the Bohai Sea.

Disruptions at choke points can be caused by conflicts and wars (Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal), terrorism and piracy (Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea, Malacca Strait between Malaysia and Indonesia), maritime accidents (Suez Canal, 2021) and environmental impacts such as drought (Panama Canal in 2019 and 2023).

But disruptions can also be intentional. At any time, around 1% of the global commercial fleet is deliberately laid up because ships are taken out of service due to economic oversupply, seasonal market dynamics or the need for maintenance and upgrades.

Economic downturns such as the global financial crisis in 2008 have led to mass vessel layups following a sharp decline in global imports and exports. Thousands of vessels — about 10% of global container vessels and 25% of refrigerated vessels – were lying idle at anchor or pulled out of service.

Large fishing fleets undergo seasonal layups associated with regulatory closures and weather-related limitations. For example, the conservation-related fishing closure in the South China Sea between May and August results in thousands of vessels laid up each year.

title.en: Tonnes of rotting food from vast LA warehouse fire creates unbearable stench
title.zh: 洛杉矶仓库大火中大量腐烂的食物散发出难以忍受的恶臭

summary.en: A fire destroyed a warehouse, leaving heaps of rotting chicken, poultry and fish to attract flies and rats.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On any typical day, Alexis Sicairos and his girlfriend have a line of patrons waiting to order a banana buzz latte or a cloud matcha at their Los Angeles coffee stand. But now, the street corner where they sit is largely empty.

On 17 June, a fire destroyed a large cold-storage warehouse in the area, leaving behind some 85 million lb (39 million kg) of rotting food, including beef, pork, poultry and seafood.

Nearly two months later, residents of Boyle Heights say the clean-up has taken a lot longer than expected, and they've grown frustrated with the pungent odour hovering over the area.

"It smells really bad, like really bad ... to the point that you want to throw up," says Mesha, a 37-year-old security guard stationed outside a marijuana dispensary.

Lineage, the company that operated the warehouse, said that as of Monday about 80% of the food waste had been removed. But city officials said this week that the company's response "has fallen short", and that they have issued public health and safety violation notices.

"It's been tough," Sicairos, 30, says. After shutting down his coffee stand for two weeks because of the fire, Brew Sting has reopened - but the demand hasn't been the same.

He says flies have been swarming relentlessly over the past weeks, since the food that was stored in the warehouse began rotting.

The warehouse workers that would previously line up to buy coffee haven't been showing up over the past two months.

"Due to the fire, obviously most of them aren't here," Sicairos says. "So we lost those customers, but we also lost customers that don't want to be around the smell, the smoke, the flies. It's understandable. But we have to keep paying our bills, so we're still here."

One cannot walk through the area, which is mostly a warehouse district surrounded by homes, without swatting away countless flies, both big and small, including black, blue and green ones.

As Sicairos packs up his coffee stand for the day, flies are landing on his tables and his body. He acknowledges that patrons don't want to see flies when they're purchasing food or drinks to consume.

A city-commissioned inspection report found that waste and high temperatures at the warehouse could speed up the breeding of flies capable of infecting wounds in both people and animals, a local NBC affiliate reported , external .

The report from a pest control company said it could put people and animals with open wounds at risk of contracting disease.

People in the community have also reported seeing large rats, and they say traps placed along sidewalks aren't big enough to hold them.

Many residents blame the city for what they deem an inadequate response to the fire and a lack of transparency and resources.

title.en: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
title.zh: 数百人因法国野火被捕，但谁应该为此负责？

summary.en: The government is trying to attribute blame for the unprecedented fires which tore through the country last month.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After wildfires caused more damage in France this year than at any time since World War Two, many are left asking a single question: Why?

A major driver is that climate is changing as a result of the well-documented way humanity is burning fossil fuels. Temperatures are only rising.

But with records showing that nine out of 10 French wildfires are started by humans, the government in Paris is trying to attribute blame - although it is itself accused of being underprepared for the infernos that have now scorched more than 300,000 acres this summer.

The interior ministry has announced 420 arrests of people alleged to have either started the fires deliberately or by accident. Among them are 166 minors.

In one case, a 23-year-old man has been accused of deliberately starting 10 fires in the space of five days in the south-eastern Var area last month. He faces 15 years in prison and a €150,000 (£128,000) fine, if convicted.

Many others have been tried and immediately sentenced, such as a man who received a three-year jail sentence for starting three recent fires in the Raon-L'Étape forest in the Vosges region.

"Only a few square metres of vegetation went up in smoke," noted L'Est Républicain, the newspaper that reported the story.

Other prosecutions have been perceived as heavy-handed and unjust. A homeless man and someone with severe autism have reportedly been handed jail terms for throwing cigarette butts.

"I was amazed at the number of arrests, it feels excessive," admits Muriel Gestas, a lawyer who has represented several people accused of arson, including two firefighters. She doubts many will lead to a conviction.

The newspaper Le Monde is also unconvinced. It questions to what extent police have examined these cases, given the short time frame.

The authorities' silence on the details - the specific charges, notably whether they involve intent and how the numbers compare with past seasons - rules out any meaningful comparison with previous years, it argues.

But Bordeaux prosecutor Renaud Gaudeul told Le Monde that a tough approach was justified by current circumstances.

"The conditions for a charge of endangering lives are met for those who throw a cigarette butt or light a barbecue in wooded areas. It only takes a tiny spark for it to start," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

"In periods of drought such as this one, all you need is a simple lighter," explains Eric Dufayet, an officer who investigates fires.

Once a fire is out, Eric's first task is to map its outline along the edge of the burnt vegetation, then trace it back to its point of origin. If the wind has been steady, that outline often forms a "V" shape. From there, his team works backwards along the path the flames took.

title.en: Joe Biden facing debilitating pain as cancer progresses, son says
title.zh: 乔·拜登之子称其癌症恶化，正面临衰弱性疼痛

summary.en: A spokesman for the former US president said in October he was undergoing radiation treatment and hormone therapy.
summary.zh: 一位前美国总统的发言人表示，他自去年10月以来一直在接受放射治疗和激素治疗。

body.en:
Former US President Joe Biden's prostate cancer has spread beyond his ‌bones and is very painful, his son, Hunter Biden, said ‌in an interview with the BBC.

"The cancer has spread, ‌metastasised into his bones and further," Hunter Biden told BBC's Newsnight, according to video posted online on Friday.

A spokesman ‌for the ‌83-year-old Democrat ⁠declined on Saturday to comment on Hunter Biden's interview.

Biden revealed in May 2025, less than four months after he left the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an "aggressive form" of prostate ⁠cancer, saying at the ‌time that it had spread to his bones.

title.en: Israel accused of weaponising archaeology at ancient West Bank sites

summary.en: Israel is planning large-scale land expropriations in historic, Palestinian areas of the West Bank.

body.en:
Up in the hills above the Roman columns of the ancient site of Sebastia, in the occupied West Bank, are olive fields that have been cultivated for generations by Palestinian families.

One of the landowners, Abu Mudif, says he has received notification that his land is part of a tranche of about 450 acres that the Israeli authorities are taking possession of in order, they say, to protect and develop the site for a major new national park.

Typically, Palestinian landowners receive little or no payment for such land expropriation. And even when it is offered, most refuse it as they see accepting it as giving recognition and legitimacy to the loss of what they see as their patrimony.

It's a vital income for Abu Mudif to lose of course, but it goes deeper than that for him.

"If I wanted to describe it, the closest description I can give is that it is like having your soul ripped away. I cannot imagine myself without my land."

He says the Israeli plan seems to be to cut Palestinian residents off from the archaeological site, which dates back thousands of years and has significant remains from the ancient Jewish past, as well as many other eras including the Romans, the Crusaders and the Ottomans.

"Restoration work has now begun along with excavations," he says. "Landowners were told that no-one would be allowed to use or plough their land."

The concerns of the village that surrounds Sebastia have been echoed by the United Nations culture and education agency, Unesco, which has now declared it not just a World Heritage Site but also added it to the List of World Heritage in Danger.

Unesco says that the main threat facing the site concerns what it calls the "planned expropriation and creation of the 'Samaria' (Shomron) national park, which could divide the property".

Standing on a path between the entrance car park in Sebastia on one side - where the Roman-era forum once stood - and the columns of the basilica on the other, the village mayor, Mohammed Azem, looks down to his right at some rubbish left in the ruins.

He says locals are now worried about reaching down to clean the area as it might cause problems with Israeli security forces and settlers.

The path on which he stands divides the site between Area B of the West Bank - which is under Palestinian civil and Israeli security control - and Area C, which is under full Israeli civil and security control.

Last week, Israel allocated roughly 113 million shekels (£27.8m) , external to expanding its control over archaeological sites in the West Bank. Some projects involve sites in areas administered by the Palestinian Authority.

title.en: New claims against Infantino deepen a turbulent period for world football's governing body

body.en:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who has endured a week of scathing criticism revolving around the now-shelved private investment plan, has been accused by a British newspaper of paying off an alleged lover while at UEFA.

According to The Telegraph, the Italian-Swiss lawyer, who served as secretary general of European football's governing body from 2009 to 2016, also previously used his influence to secure a promotion for the same UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship.

Infantino has categorically denied the allegations, according to the article, which was published on Saturday.

When contacted by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency on Saturday, a FIFA spokesperson had not responded.

According to The Telegraph, which did not cite its sources, this employee received a "six-figure sum" upon her departure — at an unspecified time — in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around £45,000 (AU$86,000).

When contacted by AFP, UEFA acknowledged that "a departure payment was made to the individual in question" at that time, "coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school".

However, it insisted "the payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time", before adding that "such regulations have been tightened since 2016".

Quoted by The Telegraph, a FIFA spokesperson stated that Infantino, who has been married since 2001, "strongly denies these allegations", which were "categorically untrue".

"Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory," FIFA added.

"No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Infantino's behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved."

Infantino, who is standing for re-election next March, has been embroiled in a crisis since the announcement late last month of his controversial — and ultimately abandoned — plan to open up the World Cup to private investors.

He faces opposition in particular from UEFA, which on Thursday stood by its threat to boycott the World Cups, deeming the mere withdrawal of the controversial plan to be insufficient.

title.en: Nigeria marries 1,500 couples in mass wedding
title.zh: 尼日利亚举行千人集体婚礼

summary.en: Nigerian authorities organized a mass wedding for 1,500 couples, stating the initiative aims to support low-income families and enhance social stability. The program included individuals who had experienced the loss of family members due to violent attacks.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚政府为1,500对新人举行了集体婚礼，称此举旨在支持低收入家庭并促进社会稳定。参与婚礼的人群中，包括那些在暴力袭击中失去亲人的家庭成员。

body.en:
The government describes the program as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability. Among those married were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

Some 1,500 couples got married at a mass wedding organized by Abba Kabir Yusuf, the governor of Kano state, in northern Nigeria .

The regional government described the two-day event as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability.

"The whole idea for the marriage is to help our families and we husbands who are not financially stable to marry; that's why the government is helping us get married," groom Abubakar Aliyu Musa told the Associated Press.

According to Kano's regional government, each bride received a dowry of 200,000 naira ($147, €127) and support to set up a small business.

The couples were also given household items including beds, mattresses and blankets.

Governor Yusuf described the program as a "bold social intervention aimed at restoring hope and supporting dignified family life in Kano."

"The program was designed not only to assist women who might otherwise struggle to afford marriage, but also to strengthen families and promote social stability in the state," he said.

Among those who participated in the mass wedding were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

One of them was Haruna Bashir, who lost his wife and six children in an attack earlier in the year. Daurawa hailed the ceremony as a step toward Bashir "gradually returning to normal life" after having "hardly interacted with people … since the tragic incident."

Nigeria has been grappling with a major security crisis for years, particularly in the country's north, which is regularly hit by raids and attacks by Islamist insurgents and organized gangs.

Many armed groups in Nigeria also kidnap schoolchildren to demand large ransoms.

On Wednesday, the Nigerian government announced the release of 308 people who had been abducted.

title.en: Iran sets conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz as talks near a critical stage

body.en:
Iran set preconditions on Saturday for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including compensation for war damages, complicating a potential deal to open the waterway essential to the world economy.

Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel initiated attacks in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage, attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route.

Continued attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire. Mediators have since urged both sides to return to the terms of a June memorandum.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Oman over transit and management of the strait were "approaching the final stages", but added the reopening of Hormuz "is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation" of the June agreement.

Security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr on Saturday laid out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including an end to the "war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq".

The comments came as transit through Hormuz has dropped significantly, with Iran targeting ships it accuses of skirting its preferred route through Iranian waters.

The United Arab Emirates' foreign ministry on Saturday condemned what it called a "hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company) with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties".

title.en: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
title.zh: 科索沃总理库尔蒂在政治危机中怂恿议会

summary.en: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.

Kosovo's parliament was suspended on Saturday after an opposition lawmaker threw eggs at caretaker Prime Minister Albin Kurti .

"Shame on you!" Time Kadrijaj of the conservative opposition Alliance for the Future of Kosovo (AAK) party shouted in parliament before hurling eggs at Kurti.

In response, Kurti said that he was "happy to pay this price" if it was the cost of dialogue.

Kurti's left-wing Vetevendosje (VV) party is known for its own parliamentary disruptions, with party representatives launching tear gas in the chamber in 2018 and also on multiple occasions in 2015.

The incident comes after days of negotiations as Kurti attempts to gain enough opposition support to elect a new president amid Kosovo's broader political crisis.

Kurti achieved his parliamentary majority with ethnic minority MPs in a December election that followed an inconclusive vote in February 2025.

His VV party's share of the vote fell from 51% to 43% in a snap election in June, but it maintained a parliamentary majority alongside ethnic minority allies.

However, Kurti requires a two-thirds majority in parliament to elect a president.

The current negotiations seem to have ground to another stalemate, with neither side having agreed to a candidate.

A constitutional deadline to elect a speaker of parliament expired on Friday. Opposition lawmakers have threatened legal action over Kurti's request for more time to negotiate.

Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 after the 1998-99 war, which ended with Serbia's withdrawal following a NATO bombing campaign.

Kosovo has been recognized by over half of the world's countries , including the United States and most European Union countries.

body.en:
Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.

The statement issued after this week's meeting in Jordan was blunt about what might happen next.

Israeli infringements on one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque in east Jerusalem, could lead to "a religious conflict with repercussions that will extend beyond the region and threaten regional and international peace and security," the foreign ministers of 10 countries belonging to the Arab League said after Wednesday's emergency meeting  in Amman, Jordan. The statement was also signed by ministers from Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, and Malaysia.

Jordan's foreign minister called the meeting because of mounting evidence that the Israeli government is surreptitiously changing a decades-old agreement meant to ensure intercommunal peace at the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, an area of great religious significance to Muslims, Jews, and Christians.

"We warn that tampering with the status quo … could trigger a religious conflict that will reverberate beyond Palestine and Jordan into the whole Muslim world," Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi told the UK newspaper  the Guardian  before the meeting.

Israel's Foreign Ministry issued a response, saying the statement was inaccurate and  Jerusalem "has never been more open and accessible to worshippers of all faiths."

Al-Aqsa is considered the third-holiest site in Islam , after Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia. The compound, also known as the Temple Mount, is also Judaism 's holiest site — two Jewish temples are thought to have stood there — and it is also of significance to Christians for its biblical connections to Jesus Christ's life.

Al-Aqsa also bears a lot of political weight because the mosque is seen by many as the embodiment of Palestinian identity, a flashpoint in a city sought as the capital of any eventual Palestinian state .

Because of the site's importance, when Israel first occupied East Jerusalem in 1967, it was deemed in the interests of Israeli national security to keep allowing Muslims to worship there. Jews could only visit and would not be allowed to pray there. Instead Jewish visitors perform religious rituals at the wall below the mosque, known as the Western or Wailing Wall.

Jordan was also allowed to continue its century-old custodianship of the site, and today the mosque is administered by a religious trust called the Islamic Waqf, paid for by Jordan at about $20 million (€17 million) annually. Israeli authorities still take care of security there.

body.en:
A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

Typhoon Dolphin raged over Japan 's southern regions on Saturday, causing some injuries and blackouts.

Okinawa and Amami island in Kagoshima prefecture were the areas expected to be worst affected.

The storm is expected to move on to China , making landfall along its eastern and southern ‌coast between late Sunday and early Monday, with Chinese authorities shutting down ports and ferry services ahead of the storm.

The China National Meteorological Centre Typhoon Dolphin has said Typhoon Dolphin will probably make landfall between the city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang province and the city of Fuding in Fujian province.

Zhejiang has raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level, while ceasing port operations and suspending 162 passenger ferry routes.

The storm is expected to bring rain and strong winds to eastern China, including parts of Shanghai, through August 12.

Some parts of eastern Zhejiang could be in for a deluge, forecasters say, with more than 600 mm (23.6 inches) of rain possible.

Ningbo ⁠Lishe ​International Airport in Zhejiang said it will stop its operations from 11:30 ​p.m. (1530 GMT) on Saturday and suspend all flights on Sunday.  

Taiwan , where 63 international flights have been cancelled, is also expected to experience heavy rain in the north over the weekend.

New political friction between Taiwan and China has also arisen after Beijing ordered that ships passing through ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed ​its traffic control instructions amid the typhoon.

Taipei has slammed Beijing's injunctions as "ridiculous," saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

"The unreasonable and crude statement ‌by ​the relevant Chinese Communist departments reflects an ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international order and norms. It is utterly ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late ​on Friday.

China regards the democratically governed island as a breakaway territory of its own and also claims to own the strategic strait, a stance rejected by both Taipei and Washington.

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin batters Japan's Okinawa before bearing down on China
title.zh: 台风海豚袭击日本冲绳，随后逼近中国

summary.en: The storm has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured five people on the Japanese island.
summary.zh: 这场风暴已导致日本岛上至少44,000栋建筑断电，并造成五人受伤。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured at least five people after hitting Japan's Okinawa island on Saturday.

Flights to and from Okinawa's main airport - Naha International Airport - were cancelled as it closed on Friday as the storm arrived.

The storm had maximum wind speeds of 162km/h (101mph) on Saturday and has been categorised as a "very strong" typhoon by the Japan Meteorological Agency, which warned of high waves, storm surges and lightning strikes.

Dolphin is expected to make landfall on China's eastern coast late on Sunday or early on Monday. Authorities there have shut ports and schools ahead of its arrival.

The main areas in Japan affected by the typhoon are the islands of Okinawa and Amami in the far south-west of the country.

Five elderly people suffered non-life-threatening injuries, according to the Okinawan prefectural government. Three of them fell because of the strong winds, it said.

Japan's national broadcaster NHK reports numerous accounts of trees being toppled by strong winds throughout Nago city in Okinawa, while a car was found overturned and leaking oil in a parking lot.

In China, Zhejiang's Ningbo Lishe International Airport said it would stop its operations from 23:30 local time on Saturday (15:30 GMT) and suspend all flights on Sunday.

A coastal typhoon alert in Zhejiang has been raised to its highest level, and port and ferry services have been halted in the Chinese province.

Typhoon season in the western Pacific typically occurs between May and October, when typhoons are considered more commonplace. This year is a strong El Niño year , which experts say means typhoons can grow to be more intense.

In an average year of 25 cyclones reaching tropical storm strength in the region, around three usually make landfall in Japan, according to the country's meteorological agency.

Some of these will be strong enough to be classified as typhoons – as was the case with Dolphin.

A typhoon is the term used for storms that form in the north-west Pacific, whereas a hurricane is the term used for storms that form in the Atlantic or eastern Pacific.
body.zh: 周六，台风“海豚”袭击日本冲绳岛后，已导致至少 44,000 座建筑物断电，并造成至少 5 人受伤。 由于风暴到来，冲绳主要机场那霸国际机场周五关闭，往返航班被取消。 周六，这场风暴的最大风速为 162 公里/小时（101 英里/小时），日本气象厅将其归类为“非常强”台风，并警告称会有巨浪、风暴潮和雷击。 预计海豚将于周日晚些时候或周一早些时候登陆中国东部沿海。那里的当局在其抵达前关闭了港口和学校。 日本受台风影响的主要地区是该国西南部的冲绳岛和奄美岛。 冲绳县政府称，五名老人受伤，没有生命危险。据称，其中三人因强风而倒下。 日本国家广播公司NHK报道称，冲绳名护市多处树木被强风吹倒，停车场内发现一辆汽车翻倒并漏油。 在中国，浙江宁波栎社国际机场表示将从当地时间周六23:30（格林威治标准时间15:30）开始停止运营，并于周日暂停所有航班。 浙江沿海台风警报已提升至最高级别，该省的港口和渡轮服务已停止。 西太平洋的台风季节通常发生在五月至十月之间，此时台风更为常见。今年是厄尔尼诺现象强烈的一年，专家表示，这意味着台风可能会变得更加强烈。 据日本气象厅称，该地区平均每年有 25 个达到热带风暴强度的气旋，其中约 3 个通常会在日本登陆。 其中一些强度足以被归类为台风——就像海豚的情况一样。 台风是在西北太平洋形成的风暴的术语，而飓风是在大西洋或东太平洋形成的风暴的术语。

reflection.en: As Typhoon Dolphin brings disruption and injury, communities face the immediate challenges of recovery. In such moments of hardship, Yahweh's word reminds us that suffering, when endured, can forge resilience and a deeper hope within us and our communities.
reflection.zh: 当台风海豚带来破坏和人员受伤时，社区面临着即时的恢复挑战。在这样的艰难时刻，雅伟的话语提醒我们，苦难若能忍受，便能在我们和我们的社区中锻造出韧性与更深的盼望。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 习近平主席从不浪费一场好危机。当伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散世界注意力时，他正在收紧控制 | 西蒙·蒂斯代尔

summary.en: The article suggests that Chinese President Xi Jinping is leveraging global distractions, such as conflicts in Iran, Ukraine, and Palestine, to consolidate power both domestically and internationally. This strategy is seen as detrimental to global order and particularly impacts minority groups within China.
summary.zh: 文章指出，中国国家主席习近平正利用伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦等全球冲突分散注意力的时机，在国内和国际上巩固权力。这种策略被认为对全球秩序有害，并特别影响到中国境内的少数民族群体。

body.en: Ever the strategist, the Chinese leader is taking the offensive, both abroad and at home. That’s bad news for global order, and minorities in his country Imagine what would happen if a British prime minister in London told the Scots they could not have their own parliament, national football team or fly the saltire. Or if the Welsh were told their language and poetry were banned and must no longer be taught in schools. The ensuing uproar would probably destroy the United Kingdom. Yet that’s exactly what Xi Jinping, China’s communist emperor, is telling the roughly 125 million members of the 55 ethnic and religious minorities who together comprise about 9% of the country’s (majority Han Chinese) population. Xi claims his sinicisation policy, embodied in a new “ethnic unity” law, will boost national identity and integration and, by expanding compulsory use of the Mandarin language, improve life and work prospects. Minorities should “hug tightly like pomegranate seeds” to build a strong, united China, he says. But Tibetans, Mongolians, Uyghurs and others who value their separate language and customs fiercely object to what they see as forced assimilation into a conformist, intolerant monoculture dominated by the Communist party’s tunnel vision. For them, it’s ethnic cleansing by another name. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...
body.zh: 作为战略家，中国领导人正在国内外发起攻势。这对全球秩序和他的国家的少数族裔来说都是个坏消息想象一下，如果英国首相在伦敦告诉苏格兰人他们不能拥有自己的议会、国家足球队或飘扬国旗，会发生什么。或者，如果威尔士人被告知他们的语言和诗歌被禁止，并且不得再在学校教授。随之而来的骚动可能会摧毁英国。然而，这正是中国共产党皇帝习近平对 55 个少数民族和宗教少数群体约 1.25 亿成员所说的话，这些少数民族加起来约占中国人口（占多数的汉族）的 9%。习近平声称，他的汉化政策体现在新的《民族团结法》中，将增强民族认同和融合，并通过扩大普通话的强制使用，改善生活和工作前景。他说，少数民族应该“像石榴籽一样紧紧拥抱”，以建设一个强大、团结的中国。但藏族、蒙古族、维吾尔族和其他重视自己独特语言和习俗的人强烈反对他们认为被迫同化为共产党狭隘视野主导的墨守成规、不宽容的单一文化。对他们来说，这是另一个名字的种族清洗。西蒙·蒂斯达尔是卫报外交事务评论员继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news highlights the profound impact of leadership on a nation and its people. When rulers tighten their grip, especially during times of global distraction, it can lead to increased hardship for vulnerable populations. Yahweh's word reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a dangerous predator over a helpless people, underscoring the deep need for...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了领导力对一个国家及其人民的深远影响。当统治者在世界分心之际加强控制时，这可能给弱势群体带来更大的苦难。雅伟的话语提醒我们，邪恶的统治者对无助的人民来说，就像危险的捕食者，这强调了对公正和富有同情心的治理的深切需求。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本，中国严阵以待

summary.en: A typhoon has struck southern Japan, causing injuries and power outages, and is now moving towards China, prompting port closures in preparation.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本南部，造成人员受伤和停电，目前正向中国逼近，中国已关闭港口进行防范。

body.en:
A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

Typhoon Dolphin raged over Japan 's southern regions on Saturday, causing some injuries and blackouts.

Okinawa and Amami island in Kagoshima prefecture were the areas expected to be worst affected.

The storm is expected to move on to China , making landfall along its eastern and southern ‌coast between late Sunday and early Monday, with Chinese authorities shutting down ports and ferry services ahead of the storm.

The China National Meteorological Centre Typhoon Dolphin has said Typhoon Dolphin will probably make landfall between the city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang province and the city of Fuding in Fujian province.

Zhejiang has raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level, while ceasing port operations and suspending 162 passenger ferry routes.

The storm is expected to bring rain and strong winds to eastern China, including parts of Shanghai, through August 12.

Some parts of eastern Zhejiang could be in for a deluge, forecasters say, with more than 600 mm (23.6 inches) of rain possible.

Ningbo ⁠Lishe ​International Airport in Zhejiang said it will stop its operations from 11:30 ​p.m. (1530 GMT) on Saturday and suspend all flights on Sunday.  

Taiwan , where 63 international flights have been cancelled, is also expected to experience heavy rain in the north over the weekend.

New political friction between Taiwan and China has also arisen after Beijing ordered that ships passing through ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed ​its traffic control instructions amid the typhoon.

Taipei has slammed Beijing's injunctions as "ridiculous," saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

"The unreasonable and crude statement ‌by ​the relevant Chinese Communist departments reflects an ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international order and norms. It is utterly ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late ​on Friday.

China regards the democratically governed island as a breakaway territory of its own and also claims to own the strategic strait, a stance rejected by both Taipei and Washington.

body.zh: 台风袭击日本南部，造成人员伤亡和停电。它现在正前往中国，那里的港口已关闭以进行准备。 周六，台风海豚肆虐日本南部地区，造成一些人受伤和停电。 预计受影响最严重的地区是冲绳岛和鹿儿岛县奄美岛。 预计风暴将移至中国，在周日晚间至周一早间在中国东部和南部海岸登陆，中国当局将在风暴前关闭港口和渡轮服务。 中国国家气象中心台风海豚表示，台风海豚可能会在浙江省舟山市和福建省福鼎市之间登陆。 浙江省已将沿海台风警报提升至最高级别，同时停止港口运营并暂停 162 条客运轮渡航线。 预计到8月12日，这场风暴将给包括上海部分地区在内的中国东部地区带来降雨和强风。 预报员称，浙江东部的部分地区可能会遭遇洪水，降雨量可能超过 600 毫米（23.6 英寸）。 浙江宁波栎社国际机场表示将从晚上 11:30 起停止运营。 （格林威治标准时间 1530），周日暂停所有航班。 台湾已取消 63 趟国际航班，预计周末北部地区也将遭遇大雨。 北京下令在台风期间通过台湾海峡的船只必须遵守交通管制指令后，台湾和中国大陆之间也出现了新的政治摩擦。 台北猛烈抨击北京的禁令“荒谬”，称北京无权限制进入国际水域。 “中共有关部门的无理、粗暴言论，体现了对国际秩序和准则的无知、无视和践踏，简直是荒谬至极！”台湾陆委会在周五晚间的一份声明中表示。 中国将这个民主管理的岛屿视为自己的分离领土，并声称拥有这个战略海峡，但台北和华盛顿都拒绝了这一立场。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.zh: 当强台风带来破坏和危险时，我们被提醒人类在大自然力量面前的脆弱。在这样的危机时刻，雅伟仍然是我们坚固的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: China’s AI ecosystem is not as open as it claims. Nor is any other country’s | Letters
title.zh: 中国的人工智能生态系统并非如其所声称的那样开放，其他国家也一样 | 读者来信

summary.en: In response to China's ambassador to the UK, experts debate the true openness of AI ecosystems, with one advocating for shared international standards and another suggesting a distinctive British approach. The discussion points to a global lack of transparency in AI development.
summary.zh: 针对中国驻英大使的一篇文章，专家们就人工智能生态系统的真实开放性展开辩论，一位专家主张制定共同的国际开放标准，另一位则提出英国可以走一条独特的道路。讨论指出全球人工智能开发普遍缺乏透明度。

body.en: Responding to an article by China’s ambassador to the UK, Prof Paul H Cleverley advocates shared openness standards, while Dr Claire Jenkins says British AI can offer a distinctive path Ambassador Zheng Zeguang rightly celebrates openly released AI models, and the Chinese labs behind Qwen, DeepSeek and Kimi have led the way – competition that benefits everyone, especially where models can run on modest hardware in the developing world ( The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together, 30 July ). But his claim that openness is a defining feature of China’s AI development deserves scrutiny. Take GeoGPT , the geoscience system from Zhejiang Lab showcased at last month’s World AI Conference as a model of jointly governed open science. It is promoted to countries as open, yet under the model openness framework – endorsed in a recent UN report – it would not qualify as open at all. It releases model weights (built mainly on Alibaba Qwen, whose licences are not Open Source Initiative-compliant), no training data or application source code is released , and its governance committee answers to Zhejiang Lab itself. Continue reading...
body.zh: Paul H Cleverley教授在回应中国驻英国大使的一篇文章时主张共享开放标准，而Claire Jenkins博士则表示英国人工智能可以提供一条独特的道路。郑泽光大使正确地庆祝了公开发布的人工智能模型，而Qwen、DeepSeek和Kimi背后的中国实验室已经引领了这条道路——竞争对每个人都有利，特别是在发展中国家的模型可以在适度的硬件上运行的地方（人工智能的未来取决于开放与合作。中国和英国可以通过合作获益良多）一起，7 月 30 日）。但他关于开放性是中国人工智能发展的决定性特征的说法值得仔细审视。以之江实验室的地球科学系统 GeoGPT 为例，该系统在上个月的世界人工智能大会上作为共同治理的开放科学的模型进行了展示。它被宣传为开放的国家，但根据最近联合国报告认可的开放模型框架，它根本不符合开放的条件。它发布模型权重（主要基于阿里巴巴Qwen，其许可证不符合开放系统互连标准），不发布训练数据或应用程序源代码，其治理委员会对之江实验室本身负责。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The global discussion on AI openness highlights a tension between national interests and the collaborative spirit needed for shared progress. While knowledge and technological advancement are powerful, Yahweh reminds us that knowledge alone can puff up, but love is what truly builds up. Genuine transparency and a commitment to shared standards can foster...
reflection.zh: 关于人工智能开放性的全球讨论，凸显了国家利益与促进共同进步所需的合作精神之间的张力。虽然知识和技术进步是强大的，但雅伟提醒我们，单有知识会使人自高自大，唯有爱才能真正建立。真正的透明度和对共同标准的承诺，能够培养信任，确保人工智能的发展造福所有人。

verse.textEn: Knowledge puffs up while love builds up.
verse.textZh: 知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，批评者担心中国可能填补外交真空

summary.en: The US State Department plans to close five foreign consulates and missions across Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia, and Cameroon. This decision has drawn criticism, with concerns that it could create a diplomatic vacuum that other nations, such as China, might seek to fill.
summary.zh: 美国国务院计划关闭在加拿大、格林纳达、日本、印度尼西亚和喀麦隆的五个领事馆和外交使团。这一决定引发了批评，有人担心这可能造成外交真空，并可能被其他国家（如中国）填补。

body.en: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. In a complex world, Yahweh's...
reflection.zh: 关闭外交使团的决定凸显了国际参与的重要性，以及撤回存在可能带来的后果。箴言11:14提醒我们，没有引导，国家就会衰落，这强调了明智的忠告和持续的外交存在对全球稳定的价值。在一个复杂的世界中，雅伟的智慧可以引导领袖们做出促进国家间和平与理解的决定。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

"There's no doubt in my mind" that the rocket "is now in teeny, little pieces scattered over the moon near Einstein Crater", McDowell said.

body.zh: 据科学家称，过去一年一直漂浮在太空中的 SpaceX 火箭的一块碎片撞上了月球。 尽管没有人观察到这次碰撞，但智利的一架望远镜发现了天文学家认为是碰撞产生的碎片羽流。 太空跟踪专家表示，剩余的火箭部分不可避免地会撞向月球。 这个校车大小的物体是 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭的第二级，该火箭于 2025 年 1 月从 Firefly Aerospace 向月球发射了月球着陆器。 这枚重 4,000 公斤的火箭原定于周三下午 4.35 左右（澳大利亚东部标准时间）撞击月球，飞行速度约为 8,690 公里/小时。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这是月球垃圾（留在月球上的垃圾）的最新实例，一些专家认为，随着美国和中国竞相将宇航员送上月球，这可能会成为一个更大的问题。 2022 年，一枚中国火箭在完成探月任务后无意中撞上了月球，而在过去的几十年里，更多的火箭碎片可能在科学家不知情的情况下撞上了月球。 SpaceX 龙人航天项目主管朱莉安娜·谢曼 (Julianna Scheiman) 表示，该公司正在与 NASA 合作，以避免未来发生残骸。 她还强调，预计的坠机事故并非故意。谢曼表示，太阳活动和重力的结合意外地使其与月球发生了碰撞。 波士顿大学行星科学家卡尔·施密特表示，他“百分百确定”他的团队的观察揭示了月球坠毁的迹象。 施密特补充说，欧洲南方天文台的甚大望远镜还探测到，在撞击发生后，钠和锂的流向太空延伸了数十公里，持续了至少五到十分钟。 施密特在与媒体分享的电子邮件中表示，“我们没有撞击的图像”，但有望远镜证据。 甚至在智利的望远镜发现碎片羽流的迹象之前，退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔就指出，周二晚上对死亡的上级的观测表明它直奔月球。 预期的坠机地点是月球阳光照射下的西翼爱因斯坦陨石坑附近一片尘土飞扬、贫瘠的地方——靠近近侧和远侧的边缘，从地球上观测到这一点尤其困难。 麦克道尔说，“在我看来，毫无疑问”火箭“现在已经变成了微小的碎片，散落在月球上靠近爱因斯坦陨石坑的地方”。 观星者知道，从地面上看到从形成的陨石坑中喷出的尘埃和岩石羽流，即使不是不可能，也是很困难的，更不用说闪光了……

title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

This pursuit of a more just world often requires courage to speak truth to...

title.en: Why economists expect the Reserve Bank to hold the cash rate this week
title.zh: 为什么经济学家预计储备银行本周将维持现金利率不变

summary.en: After months of pain, a surprise fall in inflation has buoyed hopes the cash rate will hold.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Mortgage holders will likely be able to breathe a sigh of relief with the Reserve Bank largely tipped to keep interest rates on hold.

Governor Michele Bullock and the central bank's board will meet on Monday and Tuesday, with economists forecasting the cash rate to stay at 4.35 per cent.

The prediction follows a surprise fall in inflation, despite it still being well above the bank's target band of two to three per cent.

June data revealed headline inflation fell from four to 3.8 per cent for the month, the lowest levels since the start of the Iran war.

Trimmed mean inflation, the RBA's preferred measure, remained steady at 3.6 per cent.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Senior economist at NAB, Taylor Nugent, said the RBA would likely fall into line with market forecasts.

"The RBA would need a push to deliver further tightening and the net of data flow since May has not given them that push," he said.

"Unemployment is a little above their forecast and underlying inflation marginally lower than feared."

Nugent said the RBA would likely monitor the impact of higher fuel prices on inflation following the removal of the federal government's fuel excise discount and oil prices spiking due to renewed volatility in the Middle East.

"NAB expects the next move (by the RBA) will ultimately be down, but inflation risks do remain elevated," he said.

HSBC chief economist Paul Bloxham said the central bank would likely take a wait-and-see approach before choosing to make a move on the cash rate.

"That being said, as inflation is still above target, we expect the central bank to continue to express concern that inflation is too high," he said.

"We see the downswing in growth being sufficient that the RBA begins to cut its cash rate in H2 2027."

Bloxham said there was still a chance, if inflation does not fall fast enough, that the RBA could still lift rates later in 2026.

"With trimmed mean inflation now having been above the mid-point of the RBA's target band for over four years, we see the board's tolerance for upside surprises or a slower-than-currently-projected return of inflation to target, as likely to be low."

Bullock will also face a parliamentary inquiry on Friday, where the bank's board will come under scrutiny.

Tuesday will also see fresh figures on business confidence released when NAB's latest monthly survey is unveiled.

Wall Street is meanwhile on the advance, with the US economy unexpectedly shedding jobs and amid dampened expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

title.en: Planes narrowly avoid runway collision as delays continue at Sydney Airport

summary.en: A shortage of Air Traffic Control staff has been named as the issue behind the weekend's significant flight delays.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two planes have narrowly avoided collision on the tarmac at Sydney Airport, after days of significant delays.

A Jetstar Airbus A320 was entering an intersection at around 7am on Sunday morning when it suddenly braked to avoid being hit by an incoming Qatar Airways Boeing 777 — towed by a tug.

There were no passengers aboard the Qatar plane. However, the Gold Coast-bound Jetstar flight reported the injury of a staff member.

In footage uploaded to social media from inside the Jetstar plane, the pilot can be heard updating the passengers.

"With the sudden stop, we have had a situation where one of our cabin crew has been injured," they said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The pilot told passengers that those directing the Qatar plane "didn't follow instructions".

"We were told to hold short and we were focused on crossing the runway, so only be chance at the last minute were we able to stop," they said.

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) issued a statement on Sunday afternoon, announcing it had opened an investigation into the incident.

The ATSB said it planned to collect data from both aircraft and air traffic control as part of its investigation. It will also seek to interview flight crew, ground staff and air traffic controllers on duty as well as any witnesses as the investigation proceeds.

It asked any witnesses who captured video footage of the incident to submit it via a witness form on its website.

The airport warned of delays for over 150 flights on Saturday, including 95 Qantas services.

Airservices Australia, which manages the airspace, introduced reduced traffic movements due to rostering issues.

"Airservices akcnowledged the ATFM [Air Traffic Flow Management] measures may cause some disruptions to airline scheduling and is working with airlines to reduce delays and the impact on passenger travel as much as possible," an Airservices Australia spokesperson told the ABC.

"Airservices is enhancing our training pipeline to add further controllers to improve roster depth and is working to address rostering issues that reduce the flexibility of our workforce."

Travellers also experienced delays on Friday — however were reassured by Airservices Australia that capacity had been restored and they anticipated "no further significant delays" going into the weekend.

title.en: This tiny NSW town is set to become a $560m US defence 'cornerstone'
title.zh: 这个新南威尔士州小镇将成为耗资 5.6 亿美元的美国国防“基石”

summary.en: Fifield will host the world's first primary scandium mine after a Pentagon deal aimed at countering China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A remote Australian town is set to become a "cornerstone" of the Western supply of scandium, a rare earth mineral needed for defence, planes, and data centres after local mining company Sunrise Energy Metals secured a US$400 million ($566m) pledge.

The Pentagon revealed the details of the conditional loan commitment to Sunrise to build the world's first primary mine for scandium, of which China dominates supply and processing, at a meeting between US President Donald Trump and mining executives in Washington.

Scandium is usually sourced as a byproduct of other mining and is found throughout the Earth's crust in low concentrations.

"We aim to establish Syerston as a cornerstone of Western scandium supply," Sunrise chairman Robert Friedland said in a statement, referring to the proposed mine in Fifield, New South Wales.

Fifield is a remote town in the centre of the state, roughly 450 kilometres west of Sydney. 2016 census data shows just 129 people live in the town that boasts a single pub.

NSW has some of the highest concentrations of scandium globally, Resources Minister Madeline King said.

"The Sunrise scandium project hosts the world's largest and highest-grade known scandium resource, which has a range of vital aerospace, defence and clean energy applications," she said.

"No one country alone can create secure, end-to-end supply chains in critical minerals and rare earths.

"In working together, Australian mining companies can create more jobs and investment opportunities here at home, and more jobs and investment in the United States."

King described the announcement as a "significant vote of confidence" in Australia's capacity to supply the US and its allies with the minerals they need.

China restricted exports of scandium for defence products last year, triggering the US search for new suppliers.

The Pentagon statement said the scandium project will "ensure Western alignment from mine to finished product".

"Secretary Hegseth and Deputy Secretary Feinberg are mobilizing the Department of War's resources to secure our critical mineral supply chain," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.

Trump and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signed a critical minerals agreement aimed at countering China in October, pledging that each would invest $1 billion in projects.

On Saturday, Trump announced that the US was reclaiming its place as the "minerals superpower of the world."

title.en: Wildlife under threat as bird flu spreads among natives in a second state
title.zh: 禽流感在第二个州的当地人中传播，野生动物受到威胁

summary.en: There have now been 215 confirmed or presumed positive detections of the deadly virus in Australia.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The deadly bird flu virus has spread to native birds in another state, as the national tally continues its steep rise across the country.

Two greater crested terns returned positive for the H5 flu strain in NSW, with one found near Narooma on the state's south coast and the other near Wentworth close to Mildura, officials confirmed on Saturday.

There have now been 215 confirmed or presumed positive detections, although the poultry industry remains clear of the virus so far.

It's the first time that avian influenza has been detected in an Australian native bird in NSW, with the state now recording four cases.

"These positive cases are not unexpected. We have been preparing for a situation like this, and we remain well equipped to respond to manage further impacts," Environment Minister Penny Sharpe said.

Surveillance in the impacted areas is continuing to ensure early detection of any further cases, the government added.

Testing at CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness confirmed on Saturday a further 10 detections of bird flu, all from greater crested terns in Victoria's southwest and Melbourne.

There were 28 positive detections in South Australia among wild seabirds, mostly among greater crested terns, with 15 of those on the state's Limestone Coast and 11 on Kangaroo Island, Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said.

SA chief vet Skye Fruean said there was no particular reason why the state had so far encountered most of Australia's confirmed cases.

"Unfortunately, we were just unlucky to be the first place where this did spread into our resident birds," she told ABC.

"I expect there will be other spread in other states and territories with time but ... I don't know how quickly that will happen."

Meanwhile in Victoria's southwest, avid birdwatcher Tracey Gray has been preparing alongside dedicated locals for the arrival of H5, abiding by the key advice: avoid, record, report.

Concerns grew this week when two sick birds were discovered on Port Fairy's Griffiths Island, a sanctuary for plants, birds and animals which also has a large breeding colony of short-tailed shearwaters.

While the birds, which included a crested tern and a suspected albatross, are yet to be confirmed to have the virus, the discovery is concerning.

"The (terns) are a local species that move up and down our coast from Portland, Yambuk to Port Fairy. They move, separate and nest together," Ms Gray told the Australian Associated Press news agency.

"We are concerned about them because that local transmission is potentially the largest issue here.

title.en: Kmart's Smart Glasses have sold out. Their popularity pushed a national privacy probe
title.zh: 凯马特的智能眼镜已售罄，其受欢迎程度引发了全国性的隐私调查

summary.en: Kmart's "Smart Glasses," which are surveillance wearables, have quickly sold out, leading to a national privacy investigation in Australia.
summary.zh: 凯马特（Kmart）的“智能眼镜”作为监控可穿戴设备已售罄，引发了澳大利亚全国性的隐私调查。

body.en:
The $89 Kmart alternative to Meta's artificial intelligence glasses has sold out. Its popularity has contributed to a government push to investigate privacy protections.

Released on 28 July, Anko's Smart Glasses were cleared from shelves across the country in under a week.

The product offered discreet surveillance technology to the mass market, selling for at least $200 less than premium Meta versions, which have been available for years.

The black-rimmed, clear-lens glasses can record high-definition video and snap photographs, which are then quickly transfered to smartphones.

Using HeyCyan software, users can also answer calls, listen to music and use an AI assistant.

Kmart is among many retailers, including Amazon, Temu and AliExpress, that are selling cheaper alternatives.

On Friday, the Attorney-General, Michelle Rowland, appealed to Australia's Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) to investigate the potential privacy implications of smart glasses.

Rowland requested that the independent statutory agency give the issue priority consideration, citing serious safety concerns for women and children.

"Privacy is an essential part of all our lives; it allows us to be who we are with dignity and without fear," Rowland said.

"Unlike other forms of technology, smart glasses may be used more discreetly, making it harder to know when you are being recorded.

"The OAIC regularly monitors the effects of new technologies on privacy — and the government has every faith that they will identify any new privacy risks and mitigation measures."

Rowland said the government will also continue to contribute to work to ensure "privacy laws are fit for purpose in the digital age".

According to Privacy Commissioner Carly Kind, 85 per cent of Australians have become increasingly concerned about their personal privacy since 2021.

She said that protections under the Privacy Act don't extend to those filmed by smart glasses and that new laws must be considered.

"Australia’s Privacy Act only applies to businesses and government agencies, not to individuals, and it only applies when those entities collect personal information," Kind wrote in a post to the OAIC webpage.

“In circumstances where a tech company is receiving and storing personal information collected by surveillance wearables, they’ll have to make sure they’re complying with privacy law."

However, she questioned the company's capacity to notify individuals that they are being recorded.
